title: Rafael and the Lantern
premise: Quentin Vane, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has spent nine years making himself useful and unremarkable in the port town of Saltmere. When the army requisitions the town for a staging campaign, they seize the company ledger — the only written record of every diver's debt, wage theft, and death — intending to rewrite it as proof of loyal service. Quentin, who secretly taught himself to read by copying that ledger, must steal it back and get the truth notarized before the armistice is signed, choosing between the company master who raised him and the divers who buried his father. He succeeds at terrible cost: the record stands, the master falls, and Quentin signs his own name on the last page for the first time.
about_author: N. M. Galloway is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading-company ledgers in coastal archives. Their fiction excavates the lives recorded only as line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Names
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In occupied Saltmere, Quentin keeps his head down repairing rigging while soldiers inventory the town, including the Meridian Company's ledgers. He alone knows he copied every page in secret. When he sees an officer burn a 'surplus' debt list, terror curdles into resolve: paper can be made to lie, but only if no one contests it. Emotional beat: invisibility revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with flashbacks to his father's final dive. Quentin approaches the company master, Aldous Ren, expecting an ally, and discovers Ren intends to cooperate with the army's historians — trading the true ledger for a pardon and a stake in postwar shipping. Quentin realizes loyalty to Ren was always servitude dressed as family. Emotional beat: betrayal of a father figure; the theme of corrupted power sharpens.

chapters.title: Ink Before Iron
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Racing the armistice signing, Quentin recruits the divers' widow Sefa and a sympathetic army clerk to authenticate the original ledger before a neutral notary aboard a neutral ship in harbor. Ren sets soldiers on them; the clerk dies buying time, and Quentin must choose between saving the ledger or Sefa — he saves her, nearly losing the book to the tide. Emotional beat: climax; truth demands sacrifice, not just courage.

chapters.title: Signed in His Own Hand
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The armistice stalls over disputed claims, and Quentin's notarized ledger becomes evidence read aloud in the harbor square — the divers' debts annulled, Ren arrested by the very officers he courted. Quentin declines a reward, instead asking that the ledger be archived under the divers' names, not the company's. He writes his full name beneath his father's entry. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth, quiet and hard-won.
